gloss: feudal lord; lord of a domain

definitions.gloss: feudal lord; lord of a domain
definitions.explanation: A person who rules over a territory or domain, particularly in the context of feudal Japan or medieval Europe. The lord held authority over the land and its inhabitants.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{領主|りょうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{武田氏|たけだし}だった。
examples.english: The lord of this castle was from the Takeda clan.

examples.japanese: {領主|りょうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{農民|のうみん}→農民：03759_noumin⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{年貢|ねんぐ}→年貢：16287_nengu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}めた→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧。
examples.english: The feudal lord collected annual tribute from the farmers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}→戦国時代：19200_sengokujidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{領主|りょうしゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{勢力|せいりょく}→勢力：11812_seiryoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{争|あらそ}い→争う：01866_arasou⟧、⟦{戦|いくさ}→戦：28574_ikusa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{絶|た}えなかった→絶える：13814_taeru⟧。
examples.english: During the Warring States period, local lords competed for power and battles were constant.

notes:
USAGE:
{領主|りょうしゅ} is primarily a historical term used when discussing feudal systems in Japan and Europe.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧ — a feudal lord of the Edo period, specifically a daimyo with land yielding at least 10,000 koku of rice
- ⟦{殿様|とのさま}→殿様：10455_tonosama⟧ — lord (respectful/familiar term, also used figuratively)
- ⟦{藩主|はんしゅ}→藩主：26186_hanshu⟧ — lord of a han (domain) in the Edo period
- ⟦{地主|じぬし}→地主：12048_jinushi⟧ — landowner (modern, not feudal)

{領主|りょうしゅ} is more general than ⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧ and can refer to lords of any era or country.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {領主|りょうしゅ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{館|やかた}→館：24134_yakata⟧ (the lord's manor)
- {領主|りょうしゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{治|おさ}める→治める：02462_osameru⟧ (the lord governs)
- {領主|りょうしゅ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{仕|つか}える→仕える：11547_tsukaeru⟧ (serve a lord)
